On the model {{GetCheckoutSummaryRequest}} payment method is required to get a checkoutSummary. So UI has following logic once user opens Checkout page:
- Checks if default payment method exists
- If default payment doesn’t exist, UI presents Payment Method selection screen
- If user didn’t select a payment method, he will see an error page with this text “{{Please select a payment method in order to proceed to checkout}}" and button  “{{Select payment method}}"

So if we want to change this flow, we need to make payment method optional on request for checkout summary and handle a case if user didn’t select payment method.

Thank you very much for sending the screenshots.

Let’s catch up on Wednesday to flinalise the wording.

I'm suggesting at the moment to follow the UK example, where PECR (Privacy and Electronic Communication Regulations) applies.

The marketing rules in PECR refer to “subscribers”. There are two type of subscribers in PECR- corporate and individual. So, for example, the email address or telephone number of an employee at a corporate body would constitute a corporate subscriber for the purposes of PECR because the ‘subscriber’ is their employer.

The PECR on direct marketing by electronic mail does not apply to corporate subscribers. For example, this means you can send B2B direct marketing emails or texts to any corporate body. You do not need their consent under PECR to send such messages.
However, you must not disguise or conceal your identity and give a valid address for business to opt-out or unsubscribe from your messages.

On that basis, you could go ahead with the WhatsApp communications to Admins and Business Users with no consent.

We would need though at some point to do a country by country analysis of the African legislation to ensure that the same rule applies for business contacts, as the advice we have so far is for individuals. This would requires some time though.

Let’s catch up on Wednesday please.

Hi [~accountid:5f3a47cf91e67a003f9a9427] 

Thank you for providing me with further context below and also informing me on Slack that the cancellation fee in the UK is £6.00. 

I have looked at the Driver T&Cs which state that a driver will not be legible for a cancellation fee in the following circumstances: 

_“A cancellation fee is the compensation you receive when a passenger cancels the trip after you have accepted the order or arrived at the pickup location._

_Cancellation fees do not apply if:_

* _The passenger cancels the ride less than 4 minutes after you have accepted the order_
* _You were waiting for the passenger too far from the selected pickup location_
* _You marked that you arrived at the destination when you were too far from the selected pickup location”_

By any chance do you know if the Driver marked that he arrived at the destination? and was the driver in communication with the passenger trying to locate where to pick the passenger up from? or did the driver make no attempts? 

I have listed two potential options below, however, please note, I would suggest you liaise with your manager on which option they would like to proceed with. 

*Option 1:* We are not under any obligation to provide the Driver with Bolts registered office address and trading name, therefore, you can direct the Driver to Companies House website where the driver will be able to locate this information. 

*Option 2:* If the driver arrived at the pick up location which was within a pedestrian only area, and the driver made reasonable efforts to locate the passenger, it may be worth paying the cancellation fee out on this occasion. 

+*Summary*+ 

Appreciating the fact that we do not want to set a precedent for drivers regularly claiming cancellation fees when they do not meet the threshold of receiving the cancellation fee, we need to weigh this up against if the driver makes a claim to the small claims court, the resources of defending the claim form (as a defendant who is served legal papers is obligated to respond to a claim form) may be far greater than paying the cancellation fee of £6.00. 

I also appreciate that the driver requesting Bolts registered office could be an ‘empty threat’ and the driver may have no intention at all to make a claim to the small claims court and may be saying this to get Bolt to budge and pay the cancellation fee out.  

I would suggest discussing the two options above with your manager as the decision ultimately rests with them on the best way to proceed in this particular circumstance. If you decide to go with option 1 you will have to appreciate the risk that the driver may take a claim against Bolt for the cancellation fee, and if you decide to go with option 2 and pay the the driver out in this particular circumstance I would suggest keeping an eye out to ensure this does not become a regular occurrence with this driver. 

If you wish to discuss any of the above please do not hesitate to reach out to me on Slack.

{noformat}WITH base AS (

        tt.name AS test_name,

        edasc.user_type,
        edasc.user_persona,
        edasc.city_id,
        edasc.order_id
    FROM ng_public.targeting_enrollment AS te
    LEFT JOIN ng_public.targeting_test AS tt

    LEFT JOIN ng_public.targeting_treatment AS tt2
        ON te.treatment_id = tt2.id
    LEFT JOIN ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case AS edasc

        AND edasc.created BETWEEN DATE(te.created) AND tt."end"
    WHERE te.created_date BETWEEN DATE('2023-07-25') AND DATE('2023-08-31')
        AND te.test_id = 7188
        AND edasc.id IS NOT NULL
        AND edasc.state <> 'draft'{noformat}

  , rides_price_before_discounts + rides_cancellation_fees_before_discounts + rides_no_show_fees_before_discounts AS rides_gmv_before_discounts
FROM (

    , COALESCE(subq_7.date_hour_value, subq_15.date_hour_value, subq_23.date_hour_value) AS date_hour_value

    , subq_23.rides_no_show_fees_before_discounts AS rides_no_show_fees_before_discounts
  FROM (
    SELECT
      city_id
      , date_hour_value
      , SUM(ride_price_eur) AS rides_price_before_discounts
    FROM (
      SELECT
        city_id
        , created_hour_local AS date_hour_value
        , state AS order_try_key__state
        , ride_price_eur
      FROM `dbt_silja_mardla_spark`.`etl_fact_company_order_try` fact_company_order_try_src_3

      , SUM(ride_price_eur) AS rides_cancellation_fees_before_discounts
    FROM (
      SELECT
        city_id
        , created_hour_local AS date_hour_value
        , state AS order_try_key__state

      FROM `dbt_silja_mardla_spark`.`etl_fact_company_order_try` fact_company_order_try_src_3

Thank you for providing further information below on how this feature will work operationally. We feel that the feature should trigger a new search and that the selection of the driver is random and not by default sent back to the same driver(s) who declined the journey. The reason is, we feel that this has the potential for drivers to manipulate the system/financial income. 

However, if the business would like to proceed with this feature being ‘one tap’ as opposed to a new search and including drivers who have previously declined, we would suggest that when this feature is rolled out, the business monitor if any manipulation in using the platform takes place by drivers (as we would want to avoid this occurring). Ultimately, this decision rests with the business. 

*Terms and Conditions* 

The current working under the UK Driver Terms and Conditions under Dynamic Pricing says the following:

{color:#0747a6}_“_{color}{color:#0747a6}*_Sections 18.c to 18.e will only apply when a Driver is online on the Driver App and the relevant feature is available._*{color}

{color:#0747a6}_c. Bolt UK may offer you the ability to select your preferred means of calculating the Journey Fee we pay to you for each Journey as follows:_{color}

* {color:#0747a6}*_Dynamic Pricing_*{color}{color:#0747a6}_: identified by the Bolt Platform, taking into account the estimated journey time, estimated journey distance, and any temporal, dynamic pricing variations”_{color}

We can roll with the current wording of the T&Cs for this new feature as the price is agreed between the passenger and the driver. We feel that the passenger T&Cs wording could be drafted better to fit this new feature, however at the same time passengers are not a concern for Bolt in terms of re-classification risks and manipulating the system for extra income, so rolling the feature out without amending the passenger T&Cs is a lower risk. If you feel that the passenger T&Cs should be amended to extend to address this new feature then this would delay launching this new feature as making an amendment to the T&Cs can take some time. 

We would advise discussing the above with your manager and they can make a decision on whether or not to proceed with the current wording as well as whether this should trigger a ‘new search’ or if it should be ‘one tap’.

Hi [~accountid:638713ee77acd224b3411ff9] - I appreciate your feedback, however let me explain our position regarding GDPR.

Article 6 GDPR requires that we are provided with a legal basis before we provide any data to any 3rd party, this includes the police or any other public body. the legal basis we need to establish before we provide any data is that the data must be provided as a legal necessity, not simply a request.

Article 5 GDPR requires that the data we provide is also subject to data minimisation. This is that any data provided is relevant, necessary, and proportionate to the reason the data is being requested. For us to meet the expectations of GDPR, we need to ensure that we have established that we have meet these requirements before we provide any data.

[~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] context provided below is sufficient under Article 6 for our legal basis, therefore I have no further concerns about this matter. 

If we have been able to identify the specific ride, I would suggest we provide the below information:

* User name
* User contact information
* Ride start and end location and times
* We can also confirm if the ride made any stops during its journey, how long these stops were and where they occurred

I hope the above helps clarify why we are unable to provide data immediately to the police.

Once the data has been collated, can a copy please be recorded on this ticket?

Thank you

I had a call with [~accountid:5da416c58f33800c416f2dd4] to discuss this approach.

While this approach is superficially similar to “Surge is over”, none of the “Surge is over” code could be reused for this. It has to be developed from scratch. Rough rundown of moving pieces here:

* a new service with an API to register the user’s intent of booking the busy category
* a new database to store these user intent
* a cron that checks the database periodically, collects the intents, puts them into a (new) message queue for the workers to process

{color:#006644}*Setup Required:*{color}



When you enable the Enable Advancing Unassigned Tasks check box on the Edit Tenant Setup - Business Processes task, you can easily advance an unassigned step within a business process through the:

* Advance Business Process Mass Operation Management type.
* Advance Manually related action.
* Mass Advance Business Process task.

By enabling the configuration, you can now advance:

* From an unassigned step that's pending reassignment. 
* Through an unassigned step and multiple subsequent unassigned steps.
* A business process to completion through an unassigned step that generates a reassignment during processing of the advancement.

When an event is sent back to an unassigned step, the step becomes unassigned. We add clarity to the sent back step by displaying Unassigned as the prefix to the step name instead of the name of the person in the To prompt. Example: Unassigned - Complete Questionnaire.

When Workday advances through unassigned steps, the Process History tab on the Full Process Record now displays the status of:

* Manually Advanced for the unassigned step.
* Canceled for the reassigned event.

Workday sends a notification to the:

* Business process step assignee when you advance 1 or all events to completion (except for steps that are delayed or unassigned). 
* Assignee for the manually advanced step when manual advance occurs. 

Workday doesn't send notifications when a reassigned event is canceled.

We deliver a new Enable Advancing Unassigned Tasks report field on the Tenant Setup business object (secured to the Set Up: Tenant Setup - BP and Notifications domain) that you can use to report on whether the Enable Advancing Unassigned Tasks check box is enabled on the Edit Tenant Setup - Business Processes task.

* Perform write-offs from the related actions menu on a customer invoice. 

When the machine learning model determines an anomalous value, Workday displays an alert message, enabling you to check and correct the value as you enter it.

During analysis NO issues were found on either Webpack compilation or HMR level. Its not perfect overall, but it’s configured properly and maximises the current setup.

The change in common file itself takes 6-8 seconds to update in one module, which results in 1 minute for 7 modules. So essentially there is not much big room for improvement without [offloading modules which host remote components|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-917].

One potential factor to the slow updates for both single module update (6-8s) and for the update of 7 modules, could be circular dependencies detected in {{common/campaign}}. Circular dependencies can cause Webpack to do extra work at compilation stage. There are {{61}} unique indirect circular dependencies warnings (PFA), which results in {{427}} warnings in total for 7 modules. 

Perhaps eliminating those dependencies could help.

The issue is with access token payload, we [cache it|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/common/authentication/async/service/TokenAuthenticationService.ts#L315-L326]. It is exactly {{30}} minutes in {{Live}} and {{Prelive}}. So, even the access token is refreshed, it contains stale payload. We update payload when it expires, where we check the scheduled blocks statuses in {{authProvider.getAccessTokenPayload}} [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/common/authentication/async/service/TokenAuthenticationService.ts#L334-L338], otherwise we take it from cache and cache contains "old" payload where {{blocked_until}} and {{blocked_from}} contains values and thus driver is blocked.Therefore, the question is, how we should handle it? We can decrease cache expiration time, but it will affect other parts of application, so let's not do it. Maybe, we could check scheduled block statuses in the {{src/rides/marketplace/order/main/polling/service/DriverWorkerService.ts}} instead of relying on auth token payload for {{blocked_until}} and {{blocked_from}}? Keep in mind that during {{/orderDriver/driverStartWorking}}, we always call blocking api, so we have always updated blocking status.

This is the feature from MicroMobility.

how it works:
We have several inputs into the machine engine, pretty much everything we know about the user for example:



* Information about the card (issuers, card bin, weeks to expiration, etc)
* name and last name of the client 
* IP
* Type of phone
* Type of network
* Number of related users with issues (blacklisted, chargebacks, failed payment, etc)
* What is the history of the client (number of good payments, GMV spent, etc)
* Information about the card (issuers, card bin, weeks to expiration, etc)



How it works?

For example, if we see that we have a spike in failed payments from users using iphones + Mexican numbers + Estonian network + using Japanese Cards + no payment history in Bolt and at least one related user with chargebacks, we can create rules to add friction to those clients, the type of friction will be depending on the severity of the issue, we can add low pre-auth, medium or high.





The full documentation about how dynamic pre-auths in bolt drive is here.

{noformat}-- Get all the orders from the last 15 days by the gps locations
WITH all_orders AS (
SELECT DISTINCT co.country, co.city_id, co.created_date, co.user_id, co.id, co.campaign_code, round(co.gps_lat,4) AS lat_4
, round(co.gps_lng,4) AS lng_4, CASE WHEN uu.phone_anonymized = '0del' THEN true else false END AS deleted_user
, DATEDIFF(day, uu.created_date, co.created_date) AS user_age
FROM ng_public_spark.company_order AS co  
JOIN ng_public_spark.user_user AS uu 
  ON (uu.id = co.user_id)
WHERE true 
  AND co.created_date >= DATEADD(day,-15,current_date)
  AND co.state = 'finished'
)
-- Calculate the stats for each of the locations 
, gps_stats AS (
SELECT substr(lat_4, 1, length(lat_4) - 0) || ':' || substr(lng_4, 1, length(lng_4) - 0) || ':' || country AS key 
, approx_count_distinct(user_id) AS count_total_users, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN campaign_code is not null THEN user_id end) AS count_campaign_users 
, approx_percentile(user_age, 0.5) AS p50_user_age, approx_percentile(user_age, 0.25) AS p25_user_age
, approx_count_distinct(CASE WHEN deleted_user = true THEN user_id end) AS count_deleted_users--, avg(user_risk) AS avg_user_risk
, approx_count_distinct(campaign_code) AS DISTINCT_campaigns_used
FROM all_orders AS ao 
WHERE true 
  AND lat_4 is not null  
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 desc 
)
-- Select the locations that have some minimum thresholds
SELECT *
FROM gps_stats AS gs
WHERE true 
  AND gs.count_campaign_users >= 4
  and (gs.count_campaign_users/count_total_users) >= 0.8
  and gs.p25_user_age < 10{noformat}

Hi Stephen,
Here is the information that our legal counsel has summarised for us. Our reply you will find after the summary.


We have already gathered the input from a criminal law and a data protection point of view and inform you as follows:

Is there a legal obligation compelling us to fulfil the expansive information request made by the police?

 Whether there is an obligation to provide information, depends on the legal provision on which the police bases its request. However, the correspondence at hand does not mention any (procedural) legal provision. In general, however, the following legal provisions are possible:

* +Seizure ("++_Sicherstellung_++") of data pursuant to Section 111 of the Austrian Criminal Procedure Code+ ("ACPC"):

The criminal law authorities may order the disclosure of data in the context of seizure of data. The obligation to disclose data applies to both suspected and unsuspected persons. In the case at hand, however, such disclosure of data would require the order of the public prosecutor's office, which – to our knowledge – has not been issued.

* +Disclosure of information ("++_Auskunftserteilung über Stamm- und Zugangsdaten_++") pursuant to Section 76a ACPC+:

According to Section 76a para 1 ACPC, providers of communication services are obliged to provide certain information ("_Stammdaten_") on its users at request of the criminal investigation authorities and the public prosecutor's office. One of the prerequisites is that the information is needed for the clarification of a concrete suspicion against a specific person. However, a list of all journeys of Mr Coskun cannot be considered as an information that would have to be provided under Sec 76a ACPC.

* +Enquiries ("++_Erkundigungen_++") pursuant to Section 151 et seqq ACPC:+

Enquiries serve to clarify a criminal offence and to prepare the taking of evidence. Information may only be provided on voluntary basis and must not be coerced unless it is to be provided on basis of a certain legal obligation. Such legal obligations may derive from civil or administrative obligations.

The correspondence at hand is most likely to be considered as such a voluntary inquiry. To the best of our knowledge, there are also no applicable civil or administrative law obligations which would constitute a duty for Bolt to reply to the police.

Therefore, based on the information made available to us, *Bolt is not obligated to comply with the request*. However, as stated above, the police has not mentioned any concrete legal basis in its correspondence. Hence, if Bolt wants to be on the safe side, you may ask on which legal basis the police relies in order to be able to check its permissibility and a potential duty of Bolt to disclose and provide any further data.

Given that the initial inquiry was on an unrelated matter, to what extent does data protection law apply in this instance? Are the subsequent rides, largely irrelevant to the original allegation, within the scope of disclosure?

GDPR does fully apply to any kind of disclosure of personal data, in particular Art 6 and 10 GDPR. Thus, as long as there is no legal obligation for disclosure – which would directly lead to a sufficient legal ground for GDPR reasons – you have to do balance interests of the police, the public and the driver in order to assess, if and to what extent personal data can be freely disclosed. For the concrete scenario at hand, we do follow the above outlined approach from a GDPR perspective: Ask the police on which legal basis it relies (see our wording proposal below).

Should we choose not to comply with the information request, what are the potential legal repercussions? 

There are no legal repercussions if Bolt does not comply as the request at hand is to be considered as a mere inquiry. However, on a factual level, the police may change its approach and tries to base its request on another legal basis which indeed provides for an obligation to comply. However, as the case at hand seems to be discontinued, we don't believe that the police will do so.

Workday updates the write-off lines grid that you access when you select an invoice and click the corresponding Write-Off Lines button from the:

* Write Off Bad Debt task.
* Review and revise customer invoice write-off processes.

* Renames the Writeoff Amount field to Write-Off Amount. 
* Renames the Writeoff Reason field to Write-Off Reason. 
* Displays a Worktags field where you can select applicable worktags. 
* Displays a Balancing Worktags field when you have the balancing worktag enabled in your tenant.

Note: Workday doesn't automatically populate the write-off amount on the Apply Customer Payment task.

Workday removes these columns from the Invoices grid on the Write Off Bad Debt task: 

* Total Writeoff Amount
* Writeoff Information
* Writeoff Amount
* Writeoff Reason
* Worktags

Workday adds these columns to the Invoices grid:

* Write-Off Reasons
* Write-Off Lines

Workday also: 

* Introduces the Memo field in the Customer Invoice Information section. 
* Renames the OK button to Submit when you select invoices for mass write-offs.

*Review and Revise Write-Offs*

With this release, we expand the write-off functionality of the customer invoice review and revise process to enable you to: 

* Add a memo and attachments to a write-off.
* Add or remove write-off lines. 
* Unselect invoices that you don't want to include in the write-off.

*Write-Off Memo and Attachments*

Workday now enables you to add a memo and attachments when you write off customer invoices:

* On the Apply Customer Payment and Edit Customer Payment tasks.
* During the write-off review and revise process. 
* When writing off multiple customer invoices at once. 

 ❗️You can also add or change attachments on the existing write-off transactions. To do this, you must set up the Process: Customer Write-Off - Add/Change Attachment domain security first. 

Note: When you add a memo and attachments in the corresponding header sections, Workday displays the same memo and attachments for all write-off lines. But, you can override the write-off memo and attachments on an invoice line as applicable.

*Write-Off Memo and Attachment Report Fields*

We add these report fields on the Payable Document Writeoff business object (secured to the Public Reporting Items domain) that you can use in custom reports:

* Customer Invoice Write-Off Attachments
* Customer Invoice Write-Off Memo

It was my understanding that this table was only to be added to driver communication, following Debs message below she has said that it will also be included in flyers, trade magazines etc, can we still sign this off from legal with the current analysis? or does a further analysis need to happen (as this extends to magazines and flyers), I am conscious that this may now fall in the realms of comparative advertising, so may be worth checking the reliability of the comparison etc. 



Magdalena kindly shared her notes on comparative advertising below: 

*Comparative communication:*

* *must not be misleading* - i.e. we have to be careful with language, graphics, so that there is no manipulation of facts,
* *the comparison must be reliable, objective and verifiable* - we must do good research, construct the comparison chart well, in particular:
** the data must come from publicly available info (preferably let's make a footnote to the chart, e.g. calculation based on publicly available data in competitors' apps for route xyz, day xx.xx.xx), do not get data from other sources (e.g. from fleets or drivers) - *important!*
** we need to compare the same, i.e. pay attention to what additional charges, the standard of the car, the type of journey, etc., take into account everything that has an impact on the driver's final pay, accuracy - *important!*
** keep screenshots and other material which were the basis for the comparison - leave them as documentation - *important!*
* *must not create a risk of confusion between us and the competitor* - i.e. it must be clear when we refer to our service/ride and when to the competitor;
* *does not discredit the competitor or their services* - it has to be positive about us, not negative about the competitor - *important!*
* *we can use Uber's, FreeNow's trademark (or competitors' distinctive colours)* - only to make it clear to whom we are comparing ourselves and provided the comparison is fair, honest (see above) - otherwise we expose ourselves to accusations of unfair use of competitors' trademark.

+*AB Analysis*+ 

Further questions to ask Liam: 

# What is the event going to entail? is it a talk from ACSS? is it an interactive session? 
# What is the purpose for Bolt drivers Opting in to give their contact details to ACSS and/or drivers gauging their interest do ACSS, would this be for drivers declaring their interest in further events and/or products?

+*Are there any re-classification risks*+ 

Whilst this is an event it could be considered as providing drivers with training and upskilling their knowledge on CCTV. This could be construed as Bolt providing some form of ‘training’ to drivers and could be a potential re-classification trigger. Appreciating that local councils/regulators impose requirements on safety, Bolt could potentially argue that connecting drivers to ACSS and holding such an event is to improve public safety (for the driver and the passenger) to mitigate any re-classification arguments that Bolt are integrating the drivers into the business by providing ‘training’. 

As the training is not a mandatory requirement (Bolt cannot be seen as entering control over the drivers), and drivers have the option to opt in and are not obligated to attend, I think this poses a low re-classification risk.

+*Is there an issue that not all drivers are included*+ 

I note that this event will only be offered to drivers in the Manchester area, this could potentially be an issue, I would suggest offering this to all drivers as opposed to one particular group of drivers as it may seem like Bolt are excluding drivers that work in other cities. However, Liam has advised me that the reason this is only being offered to drivers in Manchester is because each councils requirements on CCTV varies. 

+*Summary*+ 

As the drivers have a choice on whether they attend, I do not feel that this is high risk from a worker status perspective as Bolt could be seen as upholding public safety. 

In regards to the drivers invited to attend this session, whilst Bolt could be seen as excluding drivers from other cities from attending this event, Bolt could mitigate this argument if this is a council requirement, it seems that not all councils permit CCTV, therefore this is a blocker from the particular councils regulations as opposed to Bolt excluding drivers. 

Provided that Sam Sayers is happy to sign this off from a privacy perspective and as long as Bolt allow drivers the choice to opt into this event and do not make it a mandatory requirement to attend, I think this is low risk from a re-classification perspective.

Hello Agnes! 

Appreciate you reaching out here. Before we make any decision, we would like to discuss some aspects of what you are seeing. Let’s start off on what our aim is with these reviews and potential places of concern. 

Fraud price reviews' goal is to catch fraud, lessen the number of irregular activities on/through our platform, assist with technically difficult or odd cases and essentially ensure Bolt saves money while also being compliant with our obligations towards operating. We look at the trips through the lens of “Was all done correctly”, “Should this money be paid out or moved through Bolt” and “Were the necessary steps followed by all the parties”. 

To note, many teams have introduced a lot of different important checks in the duration of the order which range from safety and sanity checks to fraud checks to pricing checks etc. So Bolt has worked on providing tools for the drivers and riders to have a safe and fair journey that also complies with our regulatory standpoints. A reminder, that our ride-hailing services require that we are the middleman to arrange the trips and manage all things in relation to it. 

This brings us to the difference in our views which we noticed might be causing confusion. Currently, in Hungary, fraud is mostly targeting trips which have not been recorded through our application as they should be. Sadly, fraudsters have figured out that if Bolt does not have a say during the trip then they have the excellent opportunity to defraud us. Not only do these trips where the customer adds a primary destination but the driver ends up driving more than double the time and length of it, not adhering to our company stance but also not going through the checks that are set up in protection for all parties, especially drivers. Hence, all trips should follow the proper procedures for conducting or updating a trip and use the app as it was intended: for example, add all the stops through the app, get our approval to continue and not arrange these matters without Bolt’s confirmation and knowledge. We can actually even go as far as to say that if the driver agrees to continue without following the proper steps, they are actively arranging private offline journeys as Bolt does not have a possibility to OK this decision as the responsible middleman. This in turn ends up causing Bolt not only significant losses through fraud but also actively undermines the regulatory and operative position we have taken in the industry. Eventually, such matters have even *the risk of costing us our licences* to operate as we are allowing unregulated trips as well as potentially moving bad money. 

{quote}To conclude, by the driver allowing and continuing the trip further without waiting for approval from Bolt (through app), he/she is actively collaborating not only in illegal activities and fraud schemes but also unregulated activities and affecting themself as well as putting Bolt, as the responsible party in managing journeys booked, in high risk and potential non-compliance. {quote}

You have mentioned that the process is costing us losses. The fraud price review process depends a lot on whether we have received the payment for the irregular trip or not. Refunds happen only in cases when the journey was not paid for or there is significant repetitive behaviour to deter (clear pattern). So shortly, Bolt did not receive the money for the trip from the customer, hence the sum would have been lost to Bolt anyway and the cost and impact to compensate the driver would have been similar if we had not done anything at all through the process in those rare special cases when odd activity can be explained. Agreed, we understand that there is an extra cost with all the parties involved in compensation cases but, again, this should be a special circumstance situation. The drivers have been provided with all the necessary tools to lessen these special cases being confused for fraud from having the option to report messes in the price review process to reporting an RDNH when confirming the price. If you are experiencing a problem with the drivers not using the options provided to them, then it is perhaps a matter you’d need to discuss further with the quality, driverx and/or supply training teams.

Further, we would add that there is some necessary expertise needed to notice and tackle fraud-related cases. In your example, [1353048439|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1353048439/1539773238], we can detect many significant flags from the customer and we see it is a clear case of someone trying to use our platform maliciously. Further, as the driver agreed to continue the journey without having confirmation from Bolt that it was OK and the customer was a reliable one to continue, the driver collaborated and engaged in these irregular activities. Hence, the driver received funds only for the portion of the trip that Bolt had confirmed and allowed (and had taken responsibility for through approval). As a take-away from it, if the driver had followed our app and the safeguards set up through there, and received confirmation to continue from us,  he would have been “cleared” of any issues due to us being the responsible party for approving that part of the trip. In another example, [1328980418|https://europe-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/1328980418/1508159696], we are able to detect potential driver-rider collaboration as well as non-adherence to the safeguards that have been set up in our Bolt app. Based on the examples, no, these were not “faulty” cases and should be reviewed with the expertise fraud team has. 

Overall, fraud price reviews offer us great insight into what schemes are current and in which volumes for the market. It is a direct link to where the fraudsters move and what they do and greatly benefits our work in the general sense with market metrics and approach. 

To visualise the impact that we are actually currently talking about for fraud price reviews in Hungary:

||*Month*||*Count of Fraud Price Reviews*||
|9    (incomplete)|5|
|8|16|
|7|26|
|6|15|

I hope you take the time to review our standpoint and provide us with feedback on the points we brought out. We are happy to continue the conversation and discuss your issues.

* There is only one source of the logic for aggregating demand / supply - the backend
* Query step is a going to be a lot simpler & faster to get the training data;

The Ireland team have asked legal team to review FreeNow T&Cs. The reason for this review, is because the Ireland team want to know what FreeNow have exactly drafted in their T&Cs which permits them to vary the Tech Fee which they charge their users.



*FREENOW TERMS AND CONDITIONS* 

*Technology Fee and Cancellation Fee*
Upon completion of a Trip, {color:#ff5630}+*FREENOW shall charge a separate technology fee which will vary depending on the Transportation Services chosen by the User (the “Technology Fee”)*+{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}*and which can be found in the Passenger Fee Policy*. T*he Technology Fee is due and payable by the User to FREENOW in addition to and concurrent with the discharge of the SPSV Fare* (and, if applicable, any Third Party Charges). T{color:#ff5630}*he value of the Technology Fee, for a specific order, will be influenced by a number of factors which may include which transportation method is ordered by the passenger, the time for which a passenger orders a ride, market conditions at the time of placing the order and/or other factors*{color}. {color:#ff5630}*The Technology Fee is levied by FREENOW in return for the successful use of the FREENOW Services and is separate from the SPSV Fare (and, if applicable, any Third Party Charges)*{color}. The Technology Fee shall be separately represented on the receipt emailed to the User following the completion of a Trip; notwithstanding this, a single charge, representing the total of the SPSV Fare, the Technology Fee and any other applicable charges (including any Third Party Charges) shall be debited from the User’s default payment method provided to FREENOW for the purposes of Pay by App.

FREENOW’s entitlement to charge the Technology Fee shall be unaffected by: (i) the use by the User of any Promotional Code in respect of the relevant Trip; (ii) the payment by the User for the Trip in cash or any other payment method as may be available from time to time; (iii) the failure of any payment method selected by the User as described in section 5.5 above; or (iv) any other action taken or statement made by the SPSV Driver completing the relevant Trip. Entitlement to the Technology Fee lies with FREENOW only; the obligation on the User to discharge the Technology Fee is owed to FREENOW alone and the agreement in respect of the same as set out in section 6.1 to 6.3 exists between FREENOW and the User only.

The Technology Fee shall be charged by FREENOW to the payment methods added for Pay by App in accordance with section 5 above. Where the User chose to pay by cash for the completed Trip, FREENOW shall automatically effect payment of the Technology Fee through another private payment method registered by the User. [~accountid:627b6b92f29dcb0068f8d1e0] and [~accountid:5f5b4a58c4fbeb0069a85669], I’ll leave the specifics of the market in Malta for [~accountid:5eda5d0647291b0b8608735a], but as a rule globally, in the intermediary model Bolt only provides a summary statement to clients and the real invoice is provided by drivers, the providers of ride-hailing services.

Invoices are official tax documents in which, for tax matters, it is recognized that a person/company provided a service and is being paid for it, with the consequent VAT eventually due. In that sense, when an invoice is issued by Bolt, the income earned is recognized in our books as Bolt’s income, and Bolt is viewed, for tax matters, as the provider of RH services. This is different from the intermediary model, in which Bolt’s sole income is the B4B service fee and Bolt is just intermediating the rides.

Based on a global approach to our business, we shall not issue invoices on the intermediary model; in this model invoices are issued by drivers/fleets to customers, not by Bolt,. Also important to note that having a single invoice issued by Bolt to customer is the main advantage of the resale model, and we should not mix the models due to their different tax/financial impact on our accounts.

If you want to report bad debts, you have to comply with the provisions under the National Credit Act (NCA) for reporting defaults . Some rules apply when reporting adverse credit information i.e

# You have to let the customers know (within the prescribed time under the NCA Regulations) +before+ any prescribed adverse information concerning the person is reported to a credit bureau. Furthermore, the NCA provides that the customer, upon being notified of the intended adverse report, has the right:
## to request a copy of evidence of the adverse information; and
## has the right (within 20 business days of receipt of evidence) to challenge the information held by the credit provider and the consumer may apply to the National Credit Regulator to investigate the disputed information.
# National Credit Regulations requires that Adverse credit reports must be submitted to the credit bureau in the form prescribed by the National Credit Regulations. 
# In addition to those that Transunion has prescribed the Guidelines for the Submission of Credit Information prescribes the specific requirements which must be complied with when reporting defaulting customers. I’ve attached them here for your benefit.

[^guideline-for-the-submission-of-credit-information-in-terms-of-regulation-19-3-of-the-ncr-gen-n-8.pdf]



Overall, we are not obliged to report creditors and can only do so as incidental credit providers but because of the requirements under the NCA about form of submission and other protocols that need to be observed, I would not proceed with this option. It will be an administrative headache and can expose us to claims if we do not follow the proper procedures prescribed by the NCA.

Checked for options we have:

* Descheduler HighNodeUtilization stratregy.
* Karpenter deprovisioning methods:
** emptiness
** consolidation

h1. Results

h2. Descheduler

Descheduler is inefficient. It just kicks Pods from underutilised nodes in the hope of K8s scheduler and Karpenter logic.

But the number of simultaneously evicted Pods wouldn’t be enough for effective EC2 type calculation.

h2. Karpenter emptiness deprovisioning method

Emptiness deprovisioning method in Karpenter is even more useless than Descheduler HighNodeUtilization stratregy.

It just removes K8s worker nodes with DS only.

It can only eliminate absolutely empty instances which is good but rarely happens on prelive and live.

h2. Karpenter consolidation deprovisioning method

Shows the best results since it takes into account Pods on more than 1 node (100 instances is hardcoded currently).

Worked not well with resources reservation in our user data script due to broken estimations.

!image-20230908-083339.png|width=100%!

* 06/09 - disabled reservations is user data script
* 07/09 - enabled consolidation

The changes you observed occurred because we were in the process of transferring data from one time-off plan to another.

Now, your annual leave balances have been adjusted to comply with the local law in South Africa, transitioning from a "calendar year" to an "anniversary year" format.

Previously, our time-off plan followed the calendar year, running from January to December, with a carryover period of 6 months, also aligned with the calendar year. According to the Client, they are unaware of the outstanding balance that carried over since they were in auto-pay. 

What happened is with the refund logic. Apparently, we did a refund for €15 for a June order in July 4th. This refund showed in July’s invoice however, we process the payment in July 30th for June’s invoice excluding this €15.  Then, in August, we did lowered the invoice for July, since we did not charge this amount in June, we took it in August 30th. 

Mathematically.

June Expense = 1987.38€

June Payment = 1972.38€

June Outstanding Balance = 15€

Refund July 15€ → Lowered the July’s expenses to 2296.15€ + June Outstanding Balance = 15€ → Payment 2311.15€. 

As you see we did not double charge, nor we double invoiced. It is just how the refund logic works.

Hi [~accountid:626bc237bae0c1006fadfd63] 

I have reassessed the situation and concluded that we are engaging in quite legally risky activity by suspending the accounts of drivers who damage the cars of car rental companies 😞 

*_Main concerns:_* 

* Art 13.3 provides that Bolt can limit access to the Bot platform if a driver violates any applicable law. In case of vehicle damage, the drivers will primarily violate the contract signed with the rental company. The violation of law is secondary. Thus, relying on 13.3 by saying that we restrict the use of the Bolt App due to law violations unfortunately seems quite far-reaching to me. 

* Neither T&C nor law grants us any right to intervene in relations between the driver and the car rental company. This incident is purely between them; we as a third party shall not be engaged at all. 

* If the driver ever goes to court stating that we have suspended the use of the Bolt App restricting his freedom to provide services, it is highly likely that the court would claim that such punishment of drivers and control of drivers' provision of services is a sign of employment. 

*_A few more options_* I could think of, but both bring the same outcome – we restrict the freedom of the driver without sufficient ground and this is an employment element

# Art 13.3 allows Bolt to block the access to platform if a driver causes harm to Bolt’s business as determined in Bolt’s sole diction. By damaging the vehicles of our partners our business could be negatively affected because fleets might become resultant to cooperate. However, practically thinking, the impact would be negligent because a few incidents could not fully terminate the cooperation. So, this is not a strong argument.
# Article 13.4. states that Bolt may suspend the driver’s account for the period of the investigation if a driver engages in fraudulent activity. We possibly could extend this clause stating that Bolt has a right to suspend the account in cases of serious suspicions that the driver acts in bad faith including in relation to Bolt’s partners. In this case, we shall ask fleets to provide evidence - some photos of damaged car and possibly communication with the driver. I am not in favour of this solution too (we are interviewing where we are not supposed to intervene) but this argumentation seems better than the previous one.  

[~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]could you please share your opinion on the above (option 2 in particular)? Is there a way we can restrict the use of the Bolt App by drivers who have damaged a car of one rental company, refused to pay, and then attempt to use the Bolt App with cars from other rental companies? The idea here is that such a driver should be allowed to continue using the app with the car rented from the fleet they caused damage to, but should not be able to use app with cars from different rental companies until they pay the repair costs to the first fleet. This suspension should only last until the driver settles their debt with the original rental company. Maybe you have faced similar problems in other markets and could advise some legal solution.

 [~accountid:626bc237bae0c1006fadfd63] *_the best approach_* would be for the car rental company to resolve this internally. Some ideas:

# Ask drivers to pay a deposit when renting a car. I understand that it is impossible to predict the repair fee, but it might provide some comfort and guarantee.
# Require drivers to have casco insurance. Although it might be costly for some drivers.
# Car rental companies could collaborate and agree not to rent cars to drivers who have outstanding repair debts with other fleets. This way, drivers will not be able to simply switch to another rental company without settling their existing debts.

[~accountid:626bc237bae0c1006fadfd63] could anything form the above be implemented by the fleets? In any event, let’s wait for [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] comments.

Uz svaku djelatnost možete pronaći kratak opis i/ili pojašnjenje izbora te djelatnosti.

 

*49.41 Cestovni prijevoz robe*

* javni prijevoz tereta u untarnjem cestovnom prometu

Prema ZPCP-u, javni prijevoz je cestovni prijevoz putnika ili tereta koji je pod istim uvjetima dostupan svim korisnicima prijevoznih usluga i koji se obavlja u komercijalne svrhe, radi ostvarenja dobiti od strane prijevoznika.

Pritom napominjemo kako sukladno ZPCP-u, pravna ili fizička osoba - obrtnik smije obavljati djelatnost javnog cestovnog prijevoza putnika ili tereta u unutarnjem cestovnom prometu ako je upisana u sudski, odnosno obrtni registar za obavljanje djelatnosti cestovnog prijevoza i ako posjeduje licenciju za unutarnji prijevoz koju izdaje nadležno upravno tijelo prema sjedištu/prebivalištu prijevoznika.

Licenciju nije potrebno imati ako je riječ o prijevozu tereta vozilima ili skupom vozila čija najveća dopuštena masa ne prelazi 3500 kg.

Dakle, ako dostavljač ima vozilo koje ne prelazi masu od 3,5 t, što uključuje bicikle, motore i automobile manje i srednje veličine, nije mu potrebna licencija za obavljanje djelatnosti javnog prijevoza.

 

* prijevoz tereta za vlastite potrebe

Zakon o prijevozu u cestovnom prometu (ZPCP) definira prijevoz za vlastite potrebe kao prijevoz osoba ili tereta koji obavljaju fizičke osobe - obrtnici ili pravne osobe kao logističku potporu svojoj osnovnoj djelatnosti, pri čemu je osnovnu djelatnost nemoguće obavljati bez tog prijevoza, a prijevozna djelatnost je samo pomoćna djelatnost te osobe u obavljanju glavne djelatnosti, te koji se obavlja pod uvjetima propisanim ZPCP-om i koji nema obilježja drugih oblika prijevoza.

Licencija nije potrebna ni za obavljanje prijevoza za vlastite potrebe, ali sukladno članku 95. ZPCP-a:

* teret koji se prevozi mora biti u vlasništvu ili prodan, kupljen, dan ili uzet u najam, proizveden, dopunjen, prepravljen ili popravljen od strane prijevoznika koji obavlja prijevoz za vlastite potrebe.
* svrha puta mora biti prijevoz tereta do ili od prijevoznika koji obavlja prijevoz za vlastite potrebe te njegovo premještanje unutar ili izvan sjedišta prijevoznika koji obavlja prijevoz za vlastite potrebe
* vozilima kojima se obavlja takav prijevoz moraju upravljati vozači zaposleni kod prijevoznika - pravne osobe, prijevoznika - fizičke osobe obrtnika ili sam prijevoznik fizička osoba - obrtnik i vozila moraju biti u vlasništvu, zakupu ili leasingu ili na neki drugi način stavljena na raspolaganje prijevozniku koji obavlja prijevoz
* prijevoznik koji obavlja prijevoz mora u vozilu imati dokaz da obavlja prijevoz tereta za vlastite potrebe (račun, otpremnicu, teretni list i sl.)

 

S obzirom na prvi uvjet iz čl. 95. ZPCP-a, ova djelatnost bi bila primjerena za slučajeve kada dostavljač plaća robu u dućanu/restoranu.

 

*52.29 Ostale prateće djelatnosti u prijevozu*

 

Ovaj razred uključuje djelatnosti koje se odnose na rukovanje teretima prije, poslije ili između pojedinih prijevoznih segmenata, konkretno prosljeđivanje tereta.

 

*56.29 Ostale djelatnosti pripreme i usluživanja hrane*

 

Prema objašnjenju NKD-a, ovaj razred uključuje usluge dostave hrane na osnovi ugovora (npr. za prijevozna poduzeća), čime bi bilo obuhvaćeno preuzimanje, prijevoz i uručenje hrane.

 

*53.20 Djelatnosti pružanja ostalih poštanskih i kurirskih usluga*

 

Prema objašnjenju NKD-a, ovaj razred uključuje usluge isporuke na kućnu adresu. Napominjemo kako se po Zakonu o poštanskim uslugama taj zakon ne odnosi na kurirske usluge.

 

Best regards,

Iva

Unfortunately, the labour inspection advised us to apply employment law working time restrictions (please see the reply attached to the previous message), it followed up with this email: _“Thank you for your letter. We understand that Bolt does not employ drivers. In our previous letter, we explained working and rest times according to Employment Contracts Act and Road Traffic Act because other laws that apply to provision of services do not regulate working and rest times at all. Therefore you can apply the previously explained principles to drivers in Bolt as well if you wish to contribute to road safety and ensure that drivers get enough rest“_ 😞 

The Labor inspection suggests the following:

* driving shall not exceed 9 h, it may be extended to 10h max 2x per week;
* after a driving period of 4.5 h, the driver must take an uninterrupted break of at least 45 min. This break may be replaced by a break of at least 15 min, followed by a break of at least 30 minutes;
* Driver’s average weekly working time, including overtime, must not exceed 48 h. 

I consider this approach too restrictive and not practical. Drivers might opt for unconventional work patterns, such as an extended shift on one day followed by a rest day, managing fatigue even though the classic 9h service provision day is not followed. Also, if we implement such a system, drivers might become very dissatisfied as they will lose not only freedom but also income due to limited service provision h (we will lose profit, too).

Thus, I still prefer the implantation of an individually targeted soft approach (especially because % of drivers who work more than 12h is small):

* sending a safety notice if a driver's online presence exceeds 9h suggesting to take a proper rest to protect a driver, passengers, pedestrians, and other road traffic participants from the potential fatigue-related risks associated with extended driving hours.
* If a driver ignores us and we continue receiving concerning feedback, only then can we block him/her for a while.

After reading the screenshots attached, this matter could have been handled better. The rider had explained on the 30.08.23 that there are two Orford Roads (one in South Woodford and one in Walthamstow). +*Options to the business*+ 

# Ignore the threats and direct the rider to companies house and if the rider wants to pursue a small claim against Bolt we can deal with that once court papers are issued. 
# Bolt to offer the rider a gesture of good will voucher taking into account this was not the fault of the rider or driver as there are two roads of the same name.

# Operationally how does the mapping work on the Bolt app, how becomes the driver was not directed to the correct Orford Road?

Confirmed the flaw of the current implementation from two sides:

* by discussing it with FE engineer from {{/getActiveOrder}} team
* by testing it on Prelive with intentionally commenting out the “once per order” logic we have right now

How it works right now:

* first {{/getActiveOrder}} call in {{DRIVING_WITH_CLIENT}} state: we're sending our banner
* second call with the same conditions: we’re not sending the banner
* the FE treats the absence of banner as an indication to remove the banner from the previous call

What we can do to fix this: replace the “once per order” logic with “track dismissed state” approach. We have to send the banner with each {{/getActiveOrder}} response as long as the state is {{DRIVING_WITH_CLIENT}} (and the other prerequisites are fulfilled). Options are:

# Make the banner non-dismissable. Bad, but very easy to do. BE only, no FE changes.
# Send the “dismissed” state from FE to BE, by extending {{/getActiveOrder}} request object. Doable in reasonable time, but makes the Fav Prediction banner somewhat special, which it is not. Also requires storing the dismissed state until the next call, because the call might not happen immediately.
# Send the “dismissed” state from FE to BE in a separate endpoint. Feasible, but, again, makes the banner “special”.
# Store the “dismissed” state on FE and apply filtering to the banners FE gets in the response object. Can be done in a generic way. Amount of work unknown, but there’s a similar effort underway already: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4539450395/Active+order+information+message+extension#Message-id|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4539450395/Active+order+information+message+extension#Message-id|smart-link]

Hey [~accountid:6107b5a9b704b40068eac581],

Out team doesn’t strongly recommend it being only in Privacy Notice because it’s not compliant with the transparency obligation under the GDPR.

We propose the following:
1. *It should be clear that we share:* We clearly state on *every* screen where the feedback is requested that “Your feedback will be shared with the restaurant to improve its services. To know more about this process, please read our Privacy Policy (link to the policy)” instead of “this feedback will help the restaurant improve”.
2. *Feedback should be optional:* We include the button to skip/close the provision of the feedback, i.e., user can either “submit” or “skip/close” the feedback window. Hi team,

From a transfer pricing perspective, the *promo code cost/discount* can be +*issued*+ either by Bolt Operations *or* Local Bolt Entities. In order to decide which Bolt Entity (i.e., Bolt Operations or the Local Bolt Entity) should issue the promo code/discount, we should know to which Bolt vertical this promo code/discount refers to and which TP model is applied to that Vertical in the Local Bolt Entity.

* For instance, in the case of Bolt Thailand, the *Rides Vertical is localized* (i.e., under the localized model) and therefore the promo codes/discount for Rides should be issued by Bolt Thailand.
* However, in the case of Bolt Belgium for instance, the *Rides vertical is centralized* (i.e., under the cross border model) and therefore the promo codes/discount should only be issued by Bolt Operations (and never by Bolt Belgium). 

On the other hand, the *promo code cost/discount* should be +*booked*+ in the Bolt Entity *where the promo code is used* (regardless of where is was issued). However, similar to the one above, in order to decide which Bolt Entity (i.e., Bolt Operations or the Local Bolt Entity) should book this promo code/discount, we should know to which Bolt Vertical this promo code/discount refers to and which TP model is applied to that Vertical in the Local Bolt Entity. 

* For instance, if a Rides' promo code/discount is used in Thailand and taking into account that the Rides Vertical is *localized* (i.e., under the localized model) in Thailand, this promo code/discount should be booked by Bolt Thailand.
* On the other hand, if a Rides' promo code/discount is used in Belgium and considering that the Rides vertical is *centralized* (i.e. under the cross-border model) in Belgium, this promo code/discount should be booked by Bolt Operations (and never by Bolt Belgium). 


I hope you find this helpful. If not, please let me know 🙂 

Thanks, Sofia

# Net earnings (418.04 GBP  in the example) are *not equal* to the payout amount. In this screen, we display the *net* in-app earnings and *net* cash earnings, commission already deducted.
# The payout amount equals to the +net in-app earnings+ minus the +commission for the cash rides+ (26.78€) plus +other earnings+.
# In-app payments - *net* total of in-app payments (after commission)
# Cash payments - *net* total of cash collected from the riders (after commission)
# Other
#* Tips - total of tips (no commission is charged from tips)
#* Riders cash discounts - *net* total of cash discounts (paid by Bolt)
# Cash received - *gross* cash collected plus *gross* cash discounts minus *net* cash discounts



Please ignore the cash component, as cash is not an option in UK.

Hi, Jevgeni! Having thought about it, I think there are two legal concerns about this set-up:

# Legal relationship between the eater and the waiter 

- what is the service the waiter provides to the eater for which the eater pays? For a payment between an eater and waiter to take place, there needs to be a service. The usual approach is that the eater has a legal relationship with the restaurant who prepares the foods, brings the food to the table, etc. It’s very hard to say that e.g. eater pays for the delivery to the waiter because in cases where the eater doesn’t tip, it’s done by the restaurant.

# Acceptance of T&Cs/onboarding of waiters

 - in order for Bolt to make a payment to the waiter (ie receive payment on behalf of the waiter and transfer the tips to the waiter), Bolt would need to have an agreement with the waiter. How would this look like? I don’t think it makes sense for us to have an agreement with the waiters.

[~accountid:604aad6558aa8d00722fb03f] [~accountid:5bc9c1000e133108f3311acd] Can you take a look at the below partner invoice reissue steps? 

h3. Reissue Ghana invoices

{quote}Note that the switch date is {{2023-06-01}} and the invoice generation date was {{2023-09-04}}.{quote}

h4. 1. Delete the generated invoices in the legacy system

{code:sql}UPDATE invoice
	SET is_deleted = 1
WHERE is_deleted = 0
	AND is_source_of_truth = 0
	AND created >= DATE("2023-09-04")
	AND client_id IN (
		SELECT id
			FROM client
		WHERE external_id IN (${driverIds})
			AND `type` = "Driver"
	){code}

h5. Get driver ids

{quote}Note that Driver IDs come from the taxify_billing_ride_hailing.task{quote}

{code:sql}SELECT reference_id
	FROM taxify_billing_ride_hailing.task as t
WHERE t.state="done"
	AND t.entity_type="partner_invoice"
	AND t.reference_data = "2023-8"
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.skipped') IS NULL
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.invoice_issuer_id') in (162, 168){code}

h4. 2. Update fee and campaign bonus records invoice_id to NULL in invoicing

{quote}Note that the queries below probably should be executed in batches, because of the amount of records.{quote}

h5. Update fee records

{code:sql}UPDATE `fee` as f
	SET invoice_id = NULL
WHERE last_update >= DATE("2023-09-04") AND
	f.client_id IN (
		SELECT id
			FROM client
		 WHERE external_id IN (${driverIds})
			 AND type = "Driver"
	)
	AND is_deleted = 0
	AND invoice_id = 0
	AND sum_with_vat != 0
	AND date <= DATE("2023-06-01"){code}

{quote}Note that the above query is used to get the driver IDs.{quote}

h5. Update campaign bonus records

{code:sql}UPDATE `campaign_bonus` as cb
	SET invoice_id = NULL
WHERE last_update >= DATE("2023-09-04") AND
	cb.client_id IN (
		SELECT id
			FROM client
		 WHERE external_id IN (${driverIds})
			 AND type = "Driver"
	)
	AND invoice_id = 0
	AND sum_with_vat != 0
	AND campaign_period_end_date <= DATE("2023-06-01"){code}

{quote}Note that the above query is used to get the driver IDs.{quote}

h4. 3. Update indirect tax adjustment organic events to inactivate generated records

{code:sql}UPDATE organic_event oe
SET oe.payload_json = JSON_SET(oe.payload_json, "$.is_inactive", true),
	state = "to_execute"
WHERE oe.event_source_id IN (${eventSourceIds})
	AND city_id IN (${cityIds})
	AND entity_type = "indirect_tax_adjustment"{code}

{quote}Note that the event source ids and city ids should be fetched ahead because the query is slow.{quote}

h5. Get event source ids

{code:sql}SELECT t.id
	FROM task t
WHERE t.state="done"
	AND t.entity_type="partner_invoice"
	AND t.reference_data = "2023-8"
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.skipped') IS NULL
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.invoice_issuer_id') in (162, 168);{code}

{quote}Note that the event source for the {{indirect_tax_adjustment}} organic event is the task id.{quote}

h5. Get city ids

{code:sql}SELECT t.city_id
	FROM task t
WHERE t.state="done"
	AND t.entity_type="partner_invoice"
	AND t.reference_data = "2023-8"
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.skipped') IS NULL
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.invoice_issuer_id') in (162, 168)
GROUP BY t.city_id;{code}

h4. 4. Create reissue tasks with the updated invoice issuer

{code:sql}INSERT INTO taxify_billing_ride_hailing.task(city_id, entity_type, payload_json, reference_type, reference_id, reference_data, state, ignore_until, retry_left)
SELECT t.city_id, "reissue_partner_invoice" as entity_type, JSON_REPLACE(t.payload_json, "$.invoice_issuer_id", 172) as payload_json, t.reference_type, t.reference_id, reference_data, "to_execute" as state, NOW() as ignore_until, 5 as retry_left
	FROM taxify_billing_ride_hailing.task as t
WHERE t.state="done"
	AND t.entity_type="partner_invoice"
	AND t.reference_data = "2023-8"
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.skipped') IS NULL
	AND JSON_EXTRACT(t.payload_json, '$.invoice_issuer_id') in (162, 168);{code}

h4. 1. Update already scheduled partner invoice tasks with the correct invoice issuer

{code:sql}UPDATE taxify_billing_ride_hailing.task
	SET payload_json = JSON_REPLACE(t.payload_json, "$.invoice_issuer_id", 172)
WHERE state="to_execute"
	AND entity_type="partner_invoice"
	AND reference_data = "2023-9"

Hey [~accountid:712020:adc75bb7-f145-4fbb-b5a0-0536b95ff918]  

To zoom out from this particular transaction,

With Demand partners (DP) we *don’t* have any immediate contractual arrangement. DP’s can benefit from Bolt’s supply via Partner’s API connection with us. Partner has an agreement with us (the API agreement) and separate one’s with Dp’s.

Partner’s function can be two-fold:
1. they might serve as a mere connectivity partner facilitating the connection between the supply side (i.e. Bolt and our supply base) and the demand side (i.e. the actual rider base of DP’s), 

and

2. Partner might in addition have it’s own direct demand base as well.

_How does the above translate to privacy (contracting)?_

Until now we have been using the current annex 2 to the [template|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BS8VUWyJekCexkDFTAKopqNeYu1QvPwUMR8NdW2b5-0/edit] (fostering the controller-controller narrative), prepared by Privacy, towards the Partners under the assumption that each Partner does not only have DP’s who bring their users, but the Partners as such have their own direct demand base as well. Moreover, technically we can’t even limit the partner from requesting rides for its direct demand base as well (should it have any).

When contracting with a Partner who wouldn’t have any direct demand base, but would exclusively only be enabling access to further DP’s (and their users), should we rather opt for a controller-processor setup, and hence for a DPA (see e.g. [this here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1__0pIjswdJtiJJA_42nn3yz2eSC2oQDv/edit])?{color:#ff5630} {color}

_And as we don't really have control over the original source of the requests, should we add a clause to a DPA that if the Partner should receive direct requests, then we would be acting as separate data controllers in such circumstances?_

Happy to have a further chat on this!

A.

felix.reyes: Hola!
User has negative balance in `THB`.
Now this is the flow and what happened (very corner case)

1. First try
    a. User makes a request and fraud detects that user has negative balance but the local balance is zero, we still send the user for a low pre-auth.
    b. User has no negative balance in local currency so the final pre-auth amount is just what fraud sent.
    c. User has not that money on their card and the pre-auth fails.
2. Users puts money on the card and tries again try
3. Second Try
    a. In the background something happened, the pre-auth amount is showing as shadow credit, all shadow credit involves all debt not just local. Local debt (that never existed) now is mixed with all debt and there is no way for fraud to make a difference.
    b. Since there is still a failed amount (we do not know the currency for the second try) we sent the user for a top up.
Solution is not perfect but is pretty simple users wait a couple of seconds for the shadow balance to update and then it would be ready to order again.
This applies just to clients with foreign debt and when the first pre-auth fails.
The case for users to pay back foreign debt was escalated to balance team but it has not a strong business case.

{code:sql}with cases as (
	select
		etsc.id 														as case_id
		, etsc.order_id 												as case_order_id
		, etsc.created 												as case_created
		, co.created 													as order_created
		, co.user_id 													as case_user_id
		, edascik.issue_key
		, etsc.automation_id
		, co.city_id 													as case_city_id
		, etsc.is_solved_by_automation
	from ng_customer_support.etl_tw_support_case 							as etsc
	left join ng_public.company_order  									as co 
		on etsc.order_id = co.id 
		and etsc.city_id = co.city_id
	left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue_keys_updated  	as edascik
		on etsc.id = edascik.support_case_id
	where 1=1
		and etsc.user_persona = 'driver'
		and etsc.state in ('closed', 'solved')
		and etsc.order_id is not null
		and etsc.created_date >= date('2023-06-01')
		and etsc.created_date < date('2023-09-01')
		and (edascik.issue_key in ('rider_did_not_pay', 'driver_rider_didnt_pay_full_price')
			or (etsc.automation_id in (9, 30, 28, 73) and etsc.is_solved_by_automation = true))
),
prs as (
	select
		id 															as pr_id
		, order_id 													as pr_order_id
		, user_id 													as pr_user_id
		, order_created
		, requested_reason
		, city_id 													as pr_city_id
		, finished_by
	from ng_public.price_review_price_review
	where 1=1
		and requested_reason in ('client_did_not_pay', 'client_underpaid')
		and created_date >= date('2023-06-01')
		and created_date < date('2023-09-01')
),
base as (
	select
		c.case_user_id
		, p.pr_user_id
		, c.case_order_id
		, p.pr_order_id
		, c.case_id
		, c.is_solved_by_automation
		, p.pr_id
		, c.case_city_id

		, p.finished_by

		, finished_by 													as pr_finished_by

Here are the findings:

* We have to be concerned about the start and end dates of our invoices, once we use the user id and the period to query the data

This can be solved by using the bigger date between the date  the profile was crated and the start of the month. 
Even though we filter the received invoices by profile we don’t want to get them if we don’t need.

* We have to consider the invoice generation delay

Invoice can take some time to be generated and we never know when was the last ride before the profile is crated. To solve it, we can add a delay when processing the report task. The delay can be small if we are not worried about fiscalized invoices, if we are worried about them we need to consider the delay of 3 days that we currently have in the WP.

* Email from delete profiles

Once the profile is deleted it is not clear if we should send the e-mail to the one in the deleted profile… At the moment, using our current logic, we would use the e-mail of the rider (this includes the report)

* Report file path and name

At the moment we use the period key and the profile id. Since create a new profile with a new id we would not have problems with conflicting names. If we want to support showing reports of deleted profiles, the amount of deleted profiles can make listing data  from S3 a little bit slow. I would not worry about it, once generating reports required at least 1 ride, so deleting multiple profile and having multiple reports is even harder.

* The email template

We can use the same email template, but it does not tell that you are receiving the report because the profile was deleted, so it might also be an improvement. Current email would be sent as following, please notice that the dates in the e-mail will be relative, depending on the period the profile existed and was deleted.

{noformat}Dear Customer,

 

Thank you for using Bolt Business!

 

You will find your Work Profile monthly report from 2023-09-12 16:07:26 to 2023-09-12 16:24:35 in the attachment to this email.

 

Enjoy your rides,

Bolt Business team{noformat}


The general idea works, but we need to be aware about the invoicing generation delay and how big can the reports be in S3 (not just limited for max 12 per year).

Hi [~accountid:5f689921f0d401007029c6b0]

I have now finalised the new version that can be sent to the counterparty, see the link below and attached word document.

This version is a last push from our side with key amendments from a legal perspective. We have also explained these suggestions to the landlord in the comment section of the agreement.

*Here is a summary of our input from a legal perspective in this round:*

* *Lease term (clause 7.1 and -new- 24.3).* Given that the landlord cannot accept any premature termination rights, it's a reasonable middle way to grant Bolt a right to transfer the agreement onto an approved sub-lessee if there ever is one. We have suggested adding a new clause 24.3 to reflect this. 
+*NB:*+ Like previously discussed, please note that, although 3 years may be market practice in Norway for office leases, it is comes with great risk from a legal perspective. This could lead to us having to pay for premises that we no longer use if we for some reason have to vacate prematurely. There are use cases at Bolt where we have been locked in to office lease agreements and similar, where we are still paying for premises that are no longer used. Sub-leasing is then an alternative, but requires administration and even if we find a suitable sub-lessee, the landlord must still approve. As long as business can accept this risk, which [~accountid:5f689921f0d401007029c6b0] has confirmed via slack, we can accept it too from a legal perspective. In any event, I still recommend negotiating to get the new clause 24.3 in to mitigate this risk.

* *Indemnity clauses (5.2 and 10.7).* Ideally, we would not have the indemnity at all, but instead normal liability for direct damages (which, in contrast to indemnity, would require the landlord to prove that they have suffered any damage). However, the landlord wouldn’t accept any of our amendments reflecting this in the last round. The legal team has taken the landlord’s position into account and may reluctantly accept the indemnity obligations, but strongly advise to refrain from liability for indirect damages. Therefore, we have suggested to limit any liability in these clauses to direct damages.

* *Instructions and manuals, etc. (clause 6.5 and 12.3).* Clause 6.5 states that Bolt is automatically bound by any manuals or instructions from the Landlord. From a legal perspective, we can accept liability to follow instructions and manuals, however, only if we have had a chance to review and agree on them beforehand (because they may technically contain additional and onerous contract terms - Merlin commented in the previous round that there are use cases where Bolt has become bound by such terms through manuals/instructions in the past due to similar clauses). The landlord commented in the previous round that there are none at this point. We have made a suggested amendment entailing that any such manuals or instructions must be reviewed and accepted by Bolt before Bolt can be considered bound by them. FYI: the same applies regarding environmental certificates under clause 12.3, where we have suggested the corresponding amendment.

* *Annual rent adjustments - indexation (clause 9.1).* The landlord did not accept our previous suggestion to cap the indexation to a maximum of 5% per year. Me and [~accountid:63ee3904601ad5efa51309ee] discussed whether it would be possible to get them to accept 7% instead, given that this is the highest it’s been in 2023 so far, and I have decided that we can at least try. If the landlord doesn’t accept this, however, we accept from a legal perspective, as long as business accepts the risk of the rent increasing with over 7% per year.

* *Bank guarantee corresponding to 6 months' rent (section 11).* From a legal perspective, my conclusion is that the guarantee obligation amounting to 6 months's rent can be accepted, provided that business can accept being bound by this liability. In addition, [~accountid:63ee3904601ad5efa51309ee] has informed that it is discussed on wider level whether we should be giving out bank guarantees for security or if this should be handled with deposits instead. We need to await Merlin’s confirmation before signing. 
*FYI*: I have added a question to the landlord in a comment in clause 11.1 on whether a deposit of the same amount can be accepted as an alternative security instead of the bank guarantee. (cc: [~accountid:63ee3904601ad5efa51309ee] )

* *Bolt’s resposibility for maintanence, repairs etc (section 15).* We can accept from a legal perspective to keep the standard clauses as they are, given that this is a balanced solution according to Norwegian market practice for office leases. However, we advise to make sure that all the duties and responsibilities listed in clause 15.1 can and will be performed by Bolt in the new office.

* *Changes to the leased object conducted by Bolt (clause 17.1).* Most previous suggestions have been deleted and reverted to the standard wording. However, we recommend to at least keep that if and when the landlord accepts Bolt’s request to make a change in the office, the landlord must simultaneously decide whether such changes should be restored upon vacating or not. This will ensure that we know exactly what we need to restore when we move out, and will also help us make decisions on whether to go through with contemplated changes based on an assessment of the burden to restore when we want to leave.

* *Right to stop performing under the agreement (clause 19 and 21.3).* Clause 19 entitles only the landlord to declare himself free from all rights and obligations under the agreement if the office e.g. burns down. I suggest we try to get the same right and have suggested amendments to reflect this. The same goes for termination rights due to material breaches of the agreement under clause 21.3.


Other than the above, we have made a few suggestions for clarification purposes, e.g., in clause 8.4, 8.13, and 10.3.
